sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- lens_diagnostics: lens_diagnostics source=session reads the session cache and an empty cache is not proof of a clean file; use source=lsp scope=paths for changed files when cached findings are absent or stale
- symbol_search: Find files by identifier
- effective_config: Explain resolved configuration
- project_report: Orient in a project before choosing a file
- module_report: Outline a source module before reading a body
- read_symbol: Read one symbol's body instead of the whole file
- read_enclosing: Read the enclosing symbol or callback body for a line
- pi_lens_activate_tools: Activate a situational tool
- subagent_gate: Run subagent tasks with bounded retries and a required success quorum
- workspace_session_summaries: Inspect same-CWD session summaries before potentially overlapping repository work
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.
- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous
- workflow: Delegate substantive independent or staged work to subagents with a JavaScript workflow, optionally composing agent calls with parallel(), pipeline(), or both
- workflow_control: Inspect and manage workflow runs directly by canonical run ID.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.
- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.
- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.
- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.
- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.
- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The "Type something." row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append "(Recommended)" to its label.
- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.
- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit — do not call it; you may briefly offer it (with a rough cost) as an option instead.
- Use workflow_control for workflow lifecycle management; do not ask the user to type /workflows when this tool can perform the action.
- Use stop to terminate or quit a run. Closing the navigator does not stop a run.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description: Run a JavaScript workflow that delegates work to subagents with agent(), optionally composing calls with parallel() and pipeline().

Add phases: [{ title: 'Phase' }] only when the workflow has named phases, and declare only phases it will use. With multiple phases, call phase('Exact Title') before each phase's work or set `phase` in the agent options. Use `await workflow(savedName, childArgs)` to run a saved workflow inline; nesting is limited to one level and shares the parent run's concurrency, agent, and token limits. Optional quality helpers include verify(), judgePanel(), loopUntilDry(), and completenessCheck(). Optional control helpers include retry() and gate(); budget exposes total, spent(), and remaining(), and phase('Name', { budget: N }) sets a phase token limit. The optional `agentType` option selects a named user or project definition that can bind tools, a model, and role instructions; use it only when its name and purpose are provided in context. Its bound model overrides `tier`; an explicit `model` overrides both. Use plain JavaScript only; imports, require(), filesystem modules, Date.now(), Math.random(), and new Date() are unavailable. Use phase('Name'), agent(prompt, opts), parallel(arrayOfFunctions), pipeline(items, ...stages), log(message), args, cwd, process.cwd(), and budget. The workflow must call agent() at least once. parallel() requires functions, not promises, and returns results in input order: await parallel(items.map(item => () => agent(...))). pipeline(items, ...stages) runs stages sequentially for each item while items proceed concurrently; each stage receives (previousValue, originalItem, index).

# Implementation plan — dynamic accessibility statement

## Goal

Add a dynamic, easy-to-read accessibility statement to the website that:

- Is grouped by user need (not by report structure).
- Shows both WCAG 2.2 AAA results and WCAG 3.0 readiness results inside each
  need-based group.
- Is reachable from the top-right drop-down menu, from right-clicking the logo
  in the top left, or both.
- Carries a call to action for raising accessibility issues, whether or not
  the issue is covered by any standard.
- Is itself WCAG-compliant (it must pass the same AAA gates as every other
  view).

## Inputs consulted

- Task brief (this stage): entry points, dual AAA + 3.0 results, need-based
  grouping, universal report-a-problem CTA.
- `docs/tasks/4bda7321-3aef-4ca9-b746-42b8c6969630/SURVEY.md` — the grill-me
  survey. Note: its `answers` object is empty (no answers were recorded), so
  this plan adopts the survey's marked (Recommended) options as working
  assumptions and flags each one for one-line confirmation before build (see
  Open questions). The survey's recommended options are: top-right drop-down
  entry; five need-based groups (Seeing, Hearing, Getting around, Thinking
  and understanding, Helpful technology); dynamic = auto-updates from latest
  check results; one simple need-grouped view with both scores inside each
  group; report = short on-site form; recipient = website team by email.
- The prior-stage report `idea-20261102-093540.md` listed in the stage brief
  was not present in the task directory; only `SURVEY.md` exists there. If
  that report turns up, re-check it against the assumptions below.
- Codebase evidence: `frontend/src/routes.jsx` + `frontend/src/routing.js`
  (how to add a view), `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx`
  (`getSystemMenuItems`, the top-right System drop-down),
  `frontend/src/components/BrandMark.jsx` (top-left logo),
  `frontend/src/a11y/README.md` (app targets WCAG 2.2 AAA; WCAG 3.0 is a
  working draft — never claim conformance), `frontend/src/components/FeedbackDialog.jsx`
  (existing modal feedback-collection pattern), `canary-e2e/tests/accessibility.spec.js`
  (axe at wcag22aaa tags + AAA contrast walk over every route).

## Success criteria

1. A new `/accessibility` view exists, reachable from the top-right System
   drop-down and from right-clicking the top-left logo (right-click is
   supplementary; a keyboard-operable path always exists).
2. Content is grouped by the five user needs from the survey, in plain words,
   with each group showing its WCAG 2.2 AAA status and its WCAG 3.0 readiness
   status side by side in that group's own language.
3. "Dynamic" holds: the displayed statuses derive from the latest stored check
   results (with a visible "last checked" date), not from hand-edited prose;
   hand-written fallback copy renders only when no results artifact exists.
4. A "Report an accessibility problem" call to action is present on the page
   (and reachable without scrolling past the whole statement), opens a short
   form accepting any issue including non-standard ones, and delivers it to
   the website team inbox with a confirmation state for the reporter.
5. The new view passes `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint` (zero jsx-a11y
   errors), and the canary axe + contrast scans at the wcag22aaa tag set;
   the view is added to the e2e accessibility coverage list.
6. Docs updated: authoring guide notes the new view and results pipeline;
   statement content review cadence is recorded.

## Approach

"Make change easy, then make the change", with big/research work first:

1. **Research first (Steps 1-2).** The two unknowns that shape everything are
   the WCAG-criteria-to-user-need mapping and the shape of a "latest check
   results" artifact the frontend can consume. Both are settled before any UI
   code is written.
2. **Make change easy (Steps 3-5).** Build the enabling seams with no visible
   behaviour change: a results-data module with a fixed schema, a results
   artifact pipeline (or documented stub), and route + menu plumbing behind
   the existing patterns. Each lands with tests, independently reviewable.
3. **Make the change (Steps 6-8).** Build the statement view, entry points,
   and report form on top of those seams.
4. **Assure it (Steps 9-11).** Dedicated testing, documentation, and
   conformance-review steps close the work; nothing is declared done until
   the gates in Validation plan are green.

No new router, state library, or design system is introduced: the view uses
the existing HashRouter table, Tailwind tokens, `Modal`, `Announcer`,
`useDocumentTitle`/`titleForView`, and `GlossaryTerm` primitives.

## Steps

### Step 1 — Research: WCAG-to-user-need mapping (research, first)

- Map each WCAG 2.2 AAA success criterion the app is held to, plus the WCAG
  3.0 draft outcomes the axe "best-practice" checks approximate, onto exactly
  one of the five survey groups: Seeing, Hearing, Getting around, Thinking
  and understanding, Helpful technology.
- For each mapping row record: criterion/outcome id, plain-words summary,
  group, and which instrument verifies it (axe tag, contrast walk/gate,
  manual check, or "not auto-checkable").
- Explicitly mark everything WCAG 3.0 as draft/readiness (per
  `frontend/src/a11y/README.md`: never claim WCAG 3.0 conformance) and decide
  the honest status vocabulary for 3.0 rows (e.g. supported / partial /
  unknown — never pass/fail conformance language).
- Decide the required statement boilerplate sections (commitment, scope,
  feedback contact, review date) following W3C WAI accessibility-statement
  guidance; inspect the WAI guidance during this step and cite it in the
  mapping doc.
- Output: a short mapping document (new file under
  `docs/tasks/4bda7321-3aef-4ca9-b746-42b8c6969630/`, e.g.
  `a11y-mapping.md`) reviewed for plain-words quality. This document is the
  content contract for Steps 6-7.
- Depends on: confirmation of the five groups (survey q2; assumed yes).

### Step 2 — Research: "latest check results" source (research, first)

- Inventory what check results exist today and in what form: canary axe run
  output, the in-page contrast walk, `containerContrast` /
  `observabilityContrast` gates, lint results. None is currently persisted
  as an artifact — confirm that and decide the minimal artifact that makes
  the statement "dynamic".
- Decision to make (recommended default in brackets): [a versioned JSON
  artifact, e.g. `accessibility-results.json`, written by the accessibility
  gate run, containing per-criterion status + checked-at timestamp + app
  version; the frontend fetches it at runtime with a curated static fallback
  when the fetch fails].
- Reject (with recorded rationale): live re-scan on page open (slow, flaky,
  needs backend orchestration) and hand-edited prose as the primary source
  (violates "dynamic").
- Output: a one-page decision note appended to the mapping doc: artifact
  schema (draft), producer (which job writes it), consumer contract, and the
  fallback behaviour.
- Depends on: Step 1 (needs the criterion list to size the schema).

### Step 3 — Enabling: results-data module + schema (make change easy)

- Add a frontend module (e.g. `frontend/src/a11y/statementResults.js`) that
  owns: the results-artifact schema, parsing/validation with safe defaults
  for missing or malformed data, the criterion-to-group mapping import from
  Step 1, and selectors like "status per group per standard".
- Ship it with unit tests covering: valid artifact, missing artifact
  (fallback copy path), malformed entries (skipped, never crashing render),
  unknown criterion ids (ignored + logged), and timestamp/version surfacing.
- No UI change in this step. This is the seam Steps 6-7 build on, and it lets
  content review happen against data, not JSX.
- Depends on: Steps 1-2.

### Step 4 — Enabling: results artifact pipeline or documented stub (make change easy)

- If the producer from Step 2 is cheap (e.g. axe run already emits JSON):
  wire it to write the artifact where the frontend can fetch it, and add a
  freshness check (stale artifact = show "last checked" date honestly, never
  fake freshness).
- If the producer is expensive: ship a checked-in stub artifact generated
  from the current known-good state plus a documented manual refresh command,
  and record the automated producer as follow-up work. The statement must
  still render correctly from the stub (proving the dynamic path end to end).
- Either way, add the artifact's schema test on the producer side so drift
  breaks a test, not the page.
- Depends on: Steps 2-3.

### Step 5 — Enabling: route + entry-point plumbing (make change easy)

- Add the canonical `/accessibility` route following the documented recipe:
  `ROUTES` + `viewToPath`/`routeToView` rows in `frontend/src/routing.js`,
  `<Route>` in `frontend/src/routes.jsx`, legacy-normalisation handling,
  `titleForView` entry, and routing tests. Render a clearly-marked placeholder
  view (temporary) so plumbing can be verified before content lands.
- Add the System drop-down item via `getSystemMenuItems` in
  `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx` (unit-testable item list),
  pointing at the new route. Keep APG menu-button keyboard behaviour intact.
- Add the logo right-click path: a `contextmenu` handler on the brand cluster
  that opens the statement (and must not break the existing InfoTooltip or
  suppress the native menu without providing equivalent function — decide in
  code review whether to `preventDefault` or to offer a small custom menu;
  default: navigate on right-click AND keep the System-menu path as the
  keyboard path). Right-click is never the only path: a context menu is not
  keyboard-operable, so the drop-down entry (keyboard-accessible) is the
  primary route and right-click is a shortcut.
- Tests: routing tests, `getSystemMenuItems` test for the new item, header
  test for right-click navigation, keyboard test proving the menu path works
  without a mouse.
- Depends on: Step 3 (placeholder may import selectors, but must not block
  on content).

### Step 6 — Feature: the statement view (make the change)

- Replace the placeholder with the real statement view built from Step 3
  selectors + Step 1 copy: one section per user-need group, each showing its
  AAA status and 3.0 readiness status in plain words, with "last checked"
  date and app version in the page header.
- Authoring rules (from `frontend/src/a11y/README.md`): contrast tokens only
  (>= 7:1 text), shared `:focus-visible` indicator, `GlossaryTerm` for
  unavoidable jargon (WCAG, AAA), normal-case source copy, 44px targets,
  labelled sections and correct heading order (assert with
  `a11yTestHelpers`: `assertHeadingOrder`, `assertSectionHeadings`,
  `assertAllNamed`), route announcement via `RouteAnnouncer`, title via
  `titleForView` (view must not set `document.title` itself).
- Include a "full detail" disclosure per group linking each plain-words claim
  to its criterion ids and instrument, so the page stays simple without
  hiding evidence.
- Depends on: Steps 1, 3, 5.

### Step 7 — Feature: report-a-problem call to action + form (make the change)

- Place the CTA high on the page (visible without scrolling the full
  statement) and repeat it at the end. CTA opens a short on-site form
  (survey q5 recommended option), reusing the `Modal` + labelled-field
  patterns from `FeedbackDialog` (visible labels, named errors with fix
  suggestions, single-flight submit guard, confirmation state).
- The form must explicitly invite issues "whether or not they are covered by
  accessibility standards" and accept free text (no criterion picker as a
  required field; an optional "what were you trying to do" need-group picker
  may aid triage but must never gate submission).
- Delivery (survey q6 recommended: website team by email): add a minimal API
  endpoint (e.g. `POST /api/accessibility/feedback`) with validation, rate
  limiting, and no PII beyond what the reporter volunteers; recipient inbox
  from server config/env. Provide a `mailto:` fallback link on the form when
  the endpoint is unreachable, so reporting never dead-ends.
- Anti-abuse minimum: rate limit + payload size cap; no public issue list in
  this slice (survey option, not recommended — record as possible follow-up).
- Depends on: Step 6 (placement), Step 1 (need-group labels for triage
  picker). Confirm recipient inbox owner before build.

### Step 8 — Feature: footer link (small, conditional)

- Survey q1 option 4 offers "also add a link at the bottom of every page".
  If the app has a global footer surface, add an "Accessibility" link there
  pointing at the same route (cheap, high discoverability, standard
  practice). If there is no global footer, skip and record why — do not build
  a new footer for this task.
- Depends on: Step 5.

### Step 9 — Assurance: testing (definition of done, not an afterthought)

- Unit/integration: `npm run test:unit` green, including new tests from Steps
  3-8 (schema parsing, routing, menu item, right-click, form validation and
  submit states, API endpoint validation + rate limit).
- Static: `npm run lint` with zero jsx-a11y errors on new source; contrast
  gates still pass (no new raw-hex text colours).
- E2E accessibility: extend `canary-e2e/tests/accessibility.spec.js`
  coverage to `/accessibility` (axe at wcag22aaa tags + contrast walk),
  including the report form open state; run the spec on the scratch stack
  per its header rules (never live).
- Behavioural checks (headless, no long-lived servers): keyboard-only walk
  of menu path → statement → form submit via existing test runners/fixtures;
  right-click navigation test; malformed/missing artifact rendering tests;
  `npm run capture:screenshot` for the statement view at desktop and mobile
  widths if visual review is needed.
- Manual (one pass, recorded): screen-reader skim of group headings and
  statuses; reduced-motion and zoom (200%) sanity; mailto fallback with API
  stopped.
- Depends on: Steps 6-8.

### Step 10 — Assurance: documentation

- Update `frontend/src/a11y/README.md`: the new view, its content contract
  (mapping doc), the results-artifact pipeline and refresh cadence, and how
  to extend coverage when criteria change.
- Record the statement review cadence (who re-checks plain-words copy and
  mapping after WCAG 3.0 draft updates; suggested: each minor release or when
  the draft materially changes) in the mapping doc or team runbook.
- Add/refresh API docs for the feedback endpoint (request shape, validation,
  rate limits, inbox config) wherever sibling endpoints are documented.
- Depends on: Steps 6-7, 9.

### Step 11 — Assurance: conformance and plain-words review

- A second pair of eyes (or the task's review stage) checks: every displayed
  status traces to an instrument or is honestly labelled manual/unknown; no
  WCAG 3.0 conformance claim appears anywhere; copy reads at plain-words
  level; the CTA invites non-standard issues explicitly.
- Fix findings, re-run Step 9 gates, then close.
- Depends on: Steps 9-10.

## Validation plan (per-step evidence)

| Step | Check | Expected evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mapping doc reviewed | `a11y-mapping.md` exists; every criterion has a group + instrument; 3.0 rows use readiness vocabulary |
| 2 | Decision note | Producer/consumer contract + schema draft recorded; rejected options have rationale |
| 3 | `npm run test:unit` (frontend slice) | New schema/parser tests pass; malformed input never crashes |
| 4 | Producer test + fetch test | Schema test on producer side green; view renders from stub artifact with honest date |
| 5 | `npm run test:unit` + lint | Routing/menu/right-click/keyboard tests pass; zero jsx-a11y errors |
| 6 | Unit + `capture:screenshot` | Helper assertions pass; desktop + mobile screenshots show five groups with dual statuses |
| 7 | Unit + API tests | Form validation/submit/confirmation tests pass; endpoint validation + rate-limit tests pass; mailto fallback present |
| 8 | Unit test or skip-note | Footer link test green, or a one-line record of why skipped |
| 9 | Full gates | `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, canary accessibility spec incl. new route — all green |
| 10 | Docs diff | README + API docs + cadence note present and linked |
| 11 | Review sign-off | Traceability + no-3.0-claim + plain-words checks recorded |

Highest-risk validation: Step 9's canary axe run on the new view — it is the
only gate that judges the statement page against the AAA bar it claims, so a
failure there fails the feature, not just the tests.

## Risks and open questions

- Survey answers are empty: the six (Recommended) defaults are assumed. Each
  needs a one-line confirmation (entry point scope, five groups, dynamic
  source, single grouped view, on-site form, team-email recipient) before
  Step 6 starts; a "no" on any of them re-opens Steps 1-2 only, not the
  plumbing.
- WCAG 3.0 is a working draft: any 3.0 status display must avoid conformance
  language, and the mapping must be revisited when the draft moves. Mitigation:
  readiness vocabulary + recorded review cadence (Steps 1, 10).
- Right-click discoverability and platform behaviour (touch devices have no
  right-click; some browsers restrict `contextmenu` handling): mitigated by
  making the System-menu path primary and right-click a shortcut, plus the
  conditional footer link.
- Feedback endpoint abuse and inbox ownership: mitigated by rate limiting,
  size caps, and confirming the recipient + triage owner before Step 7.
- Results-artifact staleness could mislead: mitigated by always showing the
  "last checked" date and app version, and never rendering statuses without
  provenance.
- Non-goals: live re-scanning on page open; public issue tracker; a new
  global footer; remediation of existing app issues the statement surfaces
  (those become follow-up tasks, honestly listed as known issues if the
  statement would otherwise over-claim).

## Rollout

Single feature branch; Steps 3-5 land first as independently reviewable
commits with no visible change (placeholder route may ship hidden behind the
not-yet-linked route — no menu entry until Step 5 is complete). Steps 6-8 add
the visible surface. No migration or flag cleanup beyond removing the Step 5
placeholder. Rollback is a revert of the route/menu commits; the statement
has no stored user data to migrate.

# Accessibility statement — content contract (WCAG-to-user-need mapping)

**Task:** `4bda7321` · **Owner:** frontend · **Created:** 2026-11-02 ·
**Next review:** with each minor release, or when the WCAG 3.0 draft moves
materially (whichever comes first). See "Review cadence" below.

This document is the content contract for the dynamic in-app accessibility
statement (`/#/accessibility`). The statement view renders statuses from the
results artifact described in "Decision note (Step 2)" below — never from
hand-edited prose — using the plain-words summaries and need groups defined
here. Copy changes land here first, then in code.

Normative references: [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/),
[WCAG 3.0 working draft](https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/) (advisory only —
never a conformance claim, per `frontend/src/a11y/README.md`), and the
[W3C WAI guidance on developing an accessibility
statement](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning/statements/) (inspected
2026-11-02; required sections are commitment, standard applied, and contact
information; known limitations, measures taken, technical prerequisites, and
assessment approach are advised).

Working assumptions (survey answers were empty, so the survey's
(Recommended) options are adopted): entry via the top-right System drop-down
(primary, keyboard-operable) plus right-clicking the top-left logo
(shortcut); five need groups below; dynamic = auto-updates from the latest
stored check results; one need-grouped view with both result sets inside
each group; report = short on-site form; recipient = website team inbox from
server config.

## The five need groups

| Group id | Label | Plain-words scope |
|---|---|---|
| `seeing` | Seeing | Text size, colours, contrast, flashing, and motion. |
| `hearing` | Hearing | Sound, alerts, and alternatives to audio. |
| `getting-around` | Getting around | Keyboard, mouse, touch screen, focus, and timing. |
| `thinking` | Thinking and understanding | Clear words, simple layout, help, and forgiving forms. |
| `helpful-tech` | Helpful technology | Screen readers, input devices, and device settings. |

## WCAG 2.2 AAA mapping (the distinguishing set)

The app claims WCAG 2.2 AA conformance plus AAA conformance except the four
documented exemptions in `docs/accessibility/STATEMENT.md`. The table below
maps the 28 AAA-level success criteria — the set that distinguishes an AAA
claim from an AA claim — onto exactly one need group each, with the
instrument that verifies it. Statuses below are the position recorded by the
2026-10-25 full-scope re-audit; the checked-in results artifact carries
these values until a re-audit moves them.

Status vocabulary: `pass` (supported), `partial` (partly supported — a
documented exemption or known gap applies), `not-applicable` (the app has no
content the criterion can apply to, e.g. no video, no login).

### Seeing

| Criterion | Plain-words summary | Status | Instrument |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.2.7 Extended audio description | Videos with extra spoken description: the app ships no video, so there is nothing to describe. | not-applicable | Manual scope check (no media shipped) |
| 1.2.8 Media alternative | A text alternative for video: the app ships no video. | not-applicable | Manual scope check (no media shipped) |
| 1.4.6 Contrast (enhanced) | Text stands out from its background at 7 to 1 or better. | pass | axe `color-contrast-enhanced` (wcag22aaa tags) + in-page AAA contrast walk + `containerContrast` / `lightThemeContrast` / `observabilityContrast` / `terminalContrast` gates |
| 1.4.8 Visual presentation | Comfortable reading: colour and size choices, wide line spacing, no justified text. A line-length control for long text is not offered (exemption 2). | partial | Manual + theme / font-size settings |
| 2.3.2 Three flashes | Nothing flashes three times per second (seizure safety). | pass | Manual check (no flashing content ships) |
| 2.3.3 Animation from interactions | Motion started by the user can be turned off; the app follows the Reduce Motion setting. | pass | `reducedMotion` gate + global CSS collapse + manual |

### Hearing

| Criterion | Plain-words summary | Status | Instrument |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.2.6 Sign language | Sign language for video: the app ships no video. | not-applicable | Manual scope check (no media shipped) |
| 1.2.9 Live audio-only | A text alternative for live audio: the app ships no live audio. | not-applicable | Manual scope check (no media shipped) |

### Getting around

| Criterion | Plain-words summary | Status | Instrument |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1.3 Keyboard (no exception) | Everything works with the keyboard alone, with no exceptions. | pass | Canary keyboard guards + manual keyboard walk |
| 2.2.3 No timing | No time limits; nothing expires while you read. | pass | Manual (toasts pause on hover/focus) |
| 2.2.4 Interruptions | Nothing pops up and interrupts you. | pass | Manual |
| 2.2.5 Re-authenticating | Staying signed in while you work: the app has no sign-in. | not-applicable | Manual scope check (no authentication) |
| 2.2.6 Timeouts | Warnings before a timeout loses your work: the app has no inactivity timeouts and drafts persist. | pass | Manual (`taskDrafts` persistence) |
| 2.4.8 Location | You can always tell where you are (titles, navigation state). | pass | Manual + `titleForView` per-view titles |
| 2.4.9 Link purpose | Every link makes sense from its own text. | pass | axe `link-name` + `assertAllNamed` |
| 2.4.10 Section headings | Every section starts with a heading for screen-reader navigation. | pass | `assertSectionHeadings` + `assertHeadingOrder` |
| 2.4.12 Focus not obscured (enhanced) | The keyboard focus indicator is never hidden behind other content. | pass | Canary keyboard guards + manual |
| 2.4.13 Focus appearance | A clear focus ring (3px plus halo) on everything you tab to. With a very dark custom accent on a dark theme the ring can lose contrast (exemption 4; the accent picker warns). | partial | Shared `:focus-visible` indicator + `accentTokens` gate + manual |
| 2.5.5 Target size (enhanced) | Buttons and controls are at least 44 by 44 pixels. Dense data controls (filter pills, list rows) hold the 24px minimum instead, to keep lists readable (exemption 1). | partial | `focusVisibility` gate (44px floor) + `targetSize` heuristic |

### Thinking and understanding

| Criterion | Plain-words summary | Status | Instrument |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1.3 Unusual words | Unusual words are explained where they appear. | pass | `GlossaryTerm` + `uiTextConventions` gate + manual copy review |
| 3.1.4 Abbreviations | Abbreviations are expanded on first use and look-up-able everywhere. | pass | `GlossaryTerm` / `<abbr>` + manual copy review |
| 3.1.5 Reading level | Copy is written plainly. There is no automated grade-level gate yet (exemption 3); every change is reviewed by hand. | partial | Manual copy review per change |
| 3.2.5 Change on request | Nothing important changes unless you ask it to. | pass | Manual |
| 3.3.5 Help | Help is at hand: system guide, tooltips, and docs on every view. | pass | Manual |
| 3.3.6 Error prevention (all) | Important actions ask you to confirm or can be undone. | pass | Manual + form/confirm tests |
| 3.3.9 Accessible authentication (enhanced) | Signing in without solving puzzles: the app has no sign-in. | not-applicable | Manual scope check (no authentication) |

### Helpful technology

| Criterion | Plain-words summary | Status | Instrument |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.5.6 Concurrent input mechanisms | The app never locks you to one input: touch, mouse, keyboard, and assistive technology all keep working. | pass | Manual |
| 3.1.6 Pronunciation | Words that change meaning with pronunciation are marked: no such words ship, so nothing needs marking. | pass | Manual copy review |

## WCAG 3.0 readiness mapping (draft — advisory only)

WCAG 3.0 is a working draft. These rows describe readiness against draft
outcomes as approximated by today's instruments (axe `best-practice` rules
plus the gates above). They must NEVER use conformance language
(pass/fail/conformant). Readiness vocabulary: `supported`, `partial`,
`unknown`, `not-applicable`.

| Outcome id | Group | Plain-words summary | Readiness | Approximated by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text-contrast` | seeing | Text stays readable in every theme. | supported | 7:1 gates + contrast walk |
| `motion-and-flashing` | seeing | Motion follows your settings; nothing flashes. | supported | `reducedMotion` gate + manual |
| `audio-alternatives` | hearing | Alternatives for audio content: the app ships no audio content. | not-applicable | Manual scope check |
| `sound-alerts-have-text` | hearing | Sounds are decoration only: every alert also appears as text, and sounds are off by default. | supported | Manual (`soundEffects` default off + live regions) |
| `full-keyboard-operation` | getting-around | The whole app works by keyboard. | supported | Canary keyboard guards + manual walk |
| `pointer-targets` | getting-around | Touch and mouse targets are roomy; dense lists hold a smaller minimum. | partial | `focusVisibility` gate (exemption 1) |
| `plain-language` | thinking | Words are kept simple; no automatic reading-grade check yet. | partial | Manual copy review (exemption 3) |
| `error-help-and-undo` | thinking | Forms name the problem, suggest a fix, and important actions confirm or undo. | supported | Form tests + manual |
| `screen-reader-support` | helpful-tech | Screen readers get named controls, headings, live updates, and page titles. | supported | axe + `a11yTestHelpers` + `RouteAnnouncer` |
| `respects-device-settings` | helpful-tech | The app honours Reduce Motion, themes, and text-size settings. | supported | `reducedMotion` + theme/font settings |

## Group status aggregation (the rule the code implements)

- AAA status per group: ignore `not-applicable` rows. All remaining `pass`
  → "Supported". Any `partial` → "Partly supported". (A future
  `not-supported` value would surface as "Not supported"; none exists today.)
  All rows `not-applicable` → "Does not apply here".
- 3.0 readiness per group: ignore `not-applicable` outcomes. Any `unknown`
  → "Unknown". Else any `partial` → "Partly ready". Else → "Ready". All
  `not-applicable` → "Does not apply here".

## Required statement boilerplate (from W3C WAI)

The view carries these sections in plain words: commitment to accessibility;
standard applied (WCAG 2.2 AA conformant; AAA conformant except the listed
exemptions; WCAG 3.0 draft readiness shown without any conformance claim);
scope (the SPA routes, named); feedback contact (the report form plus the
team inbox address from server config); known limitations (the four
exemptions as user-facing known issues); measures taken (the gates above);
technical information (works in current browsers with JavaScript; no
plug-ins); assessment approach (automated scans plus manual keyboard /
screen-reader passes); approval and review date.

## Decision note (Step 2): the "latest check results" source

Inventory: the canary axe run emits no persisted artifact; the contrast walk
runs in-page during e2e; `containerContrast` / `observabilityContrast` /
theme gates run in vitest; lint runs in CI. None is persisted — confirmed.

Decision (the plan's recommended default): a versioned JSON artifact,
`api/accessibility-results.json`, served read-only at
`GET /accessibility/results`, containing per-criterion status +
per-outcome readiness + known issues + `generatedAt` timestamp + app
version + contact inbox. The frontend fetches it at runtime and renders
statuses from it; when the fetch fails or the artifact is missing, a
curated static fallback renders with an honest "latest results unavailable"
note. The mapping tables above are the single source of truth, shared by
both sides as `shared/accessibilityStatement.js`, so the producer and the
view cannot drift apart. A manual refresh command,
`node scripts/refresh-accessibility-results.mjs`, re-stamps `generatedAt`
and the app version after a re-audit; automating the producer (emit the
artifact from the gate run) is recorded follow-up work, not this slice.

Rejected: live re-scan on page open (slow, flaky, needs backend
orchestration for axe) and hand-edited prose as the primary source (violates
"dynamic" — statuses must derive from stored results).

Artifact schema (v1, draft — authoritative in
`shared/accessibilityStatement.js`):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedAt": "<ISO timestamp>",
  "appVersion": "<string>",
  "contactEmail": "<team inbox or empty when unconfigured>",
  "wcag22aaa": [{ "criterion": "1.4.6", "status": "pass", "evidence": "<short>" }],
  "wcag30": [{ "outcome": "text-contrast", "readiness": "supported", "note": "<short>" }],
  "knownIssues": [{ "id": "target-size-dense", "summary": "<plain words>", "group": "getting-around" }]
}
```

Fallback behaviour: missing artifact, failed fetch, or malformed entries →
curated fallback copy renders (statuses marked as last-known, honestly
dated); malformed entries are skipped, unknown criterion ids ignored and
logged, and rendering never crashes.

## Review cadence

Re-check this mapping and the plain-words copy on each minor release and
whenever the WCAG 3.0 draft moves materially; refresh the artifact stamp at
the same time. Owner: frontend. The statement view always shows its
"last checked" date, so staleness is visible, never silent.

## Step 8 decision: no footer link

Skipped with rationale: the app has no global footer surface (the only
footers in the codebase are modal footers), and building a new footer for
this task is out of scope. The statement stays reachable from the System
menu (primary, keyboard-operable), the logo right-click shortcut, and the
`A` keyboard shortcut.
